overview: This two-page file combines a corrected secret telegram from the U.S. Embassy in Nanking concerning efforts to obtain American engineering advice for Taiwan with an administrative sheet recording the transfer of a later telegram to another decimal-file classification. The telegram reports that Armstrong would provide the services of a competent firm but would not personally accept a contract requiring extended residence in Taiwan, while C. K. Yen promised to seek another American willing to serve as Wei Tao-ming’s personal adviser. It also conveys doubt that a suitable candidate could be recruited, even through Economic Cooperation Administration engineering projects, because qualified Americans knew too little about Taiwan to commit to living there for a prolonged period.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Stuart on recruiting an engineering adviser for Taiwan
subfiles.from: J. Leighton Stuart, U.S. Embassy, Nanking
subfiles.about: Reports discussions about securing either a consulting firm or a resident American engineering adviser for Wei Tao-ming in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Following Stillman’s discussions with Armstrong, the Embassy reports that Taiwan needs the services of a competent firm rather than merely a personal adviser to Wei Tao-ming. Armstrong is willing to have his firm undertake the work but refuses any personal contract requiring him to spend a definite period in Taiwan. C. K. Yen has promised to seek another qualified American, although Stillman doubts that anyone will accept prolonged residence in a place about which prospective candidates know little. The secret telegram was sent to Taipei, repeated to the Department of State, and issued as a corrected copy on August 22.

subfiles.title: Transfer sheet for Telegram No. 1564
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.about: Records the reclassification of correspondence dated August 24, 1948, from the engineering-adviser file to a general Japan file.
subfiles.summary: The Division of Communications and Records transferred an item dated August 24, 1948, from file 894.64A/8-2448 to file 800.504 Japan/8-2448 on September 23, 1948. The remarks identify the transferred item as Telegram No. 1564, although the telegram itself is not present on this page.

interest: The telegram offers unusually concrete evidence of the practical obstacles facing postwar American technical-assistance programs: prospective advisers’ limited knowledge of Taiwan, reluctance to accept prolonged residence, and the resulting preference for contracting with firms rather than individuals. It also documents the involvement of prominent Taiwanese officials Wei Tao-ming and Yen Chia-kan in recruiting foreign expertise. The transfer sheet is archivally revealing because it helps explain why Taiwan-related material appears in a file titled for Japan and shows how State Department correspondence could be reclassified after filing.
